question_text: Write the complex number (a − ib)/(a + ib) in the form A + iB.

mark_split.label: Multiply above and below by a − ib
Expand and separate A and B

recall_prompt: Say how you would write this quotient in the form A + iB — what you multiply by and what you read off.
insider_note: The multiplier is the numerator itself, so the top becomes the single expansion (a − ib)², not four separate products. The second mark is for naming A and B separately — one unsplit fraction is not the form asked.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply by the conjugate
steps.margin_note: First mark. The conjugate of the denominator a + ib is a − ib, which is also the numerator — so the top becomes (a − ib)² and the bottom becomes a² + b².
steps.memory_tip: The conjugate a − ib is the numerator itself, so the top becomes one square and the bottom a² + b².

recall.must_convey: That numerator and denominator are multiplied by a − ib, the conjugate of the denominator, giving (a − ib)² over a² + b².

steps.why: (a + ib)(a − ib) = a² − i²b² = a² + b² is real, so after this multiplication the i lives only in the numerator, where it can be separated.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by a + ib, which leaves an i in the denominator.
Writing the denominator as a² − b².

steps.label: Separate A and B
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Expand (a − ib)² = a² − 2abi + i²b² = (a² − b²) − 2abi, then split over the common denominator.
steps.memory_tip: i²b² = −b², so (a − ib)² = (a² − b²) − 2abi. The minus belongs to B, not to the denominator.
lines: so A = (a² − b²)/(a² + b²), B = −2ab/(a² + b²).

recall.must_convey: That expanding gives A = (a² − b²)/(a² + b²) and B = −2ab/(a² + b²).

steps.why: The form A + iB needs the fraction split into a real part and a real coefficient of i, each over the real denominator. The minus on B comes from −2abi, not from the denominator.
common_mistakes: Writing i²b² as +b² and getting A = (a² + b²)/(a² + b²) = 1.
Leaving the answer as one fraction without naming A and B.
